questions.stem: What are the sex chromosomes in a human female?

options.text: YY
XX
XO
XY

questions.explanation: Human females have two X chromosomes (XX). Human males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY). The sex chromosomes are one of the 23 pairs of chromosomes in human cells.

questions.stem: What is the probability of a baby being male?
questions.explanation: There is a 50% (1 in 2) chance of a baby being male. The mother always contributes an X chromosome, while the father contributes either an X (producing a girl) or a Y (producing a boy) with equal probability.

questions.stem: Which parent determines the sex of the offspring?

options.text: Both parents equally
Neither parent; it is completely random
The mother, because she produces the egg
The father, because he can contribute either an X or Y chromosome

questions.explanation: The father determines the sex because he produces two types of sperm: those carrying an X chromosome and those carrying a Y chromosome. The mother can only contribute an X. If the sperm carries Y, the child is male (XY); if X, female (XX).

options.text: A characteristic that only appears during puberty
A characteristic that is controlled by more than one gene
A characteristic controlled by a gene located on a sex chromosome
A characteristic that differs between identical twins

questions.explanation: A sex-linked characteristic is controlled by a gene located on one of the sex chromosomes (usually the X chromosome). Examples include red-green colour blindness and haemophilia, which are more common in males.

questions.stem: Why are X-linked recessive conditions like colour blindness more common in males?

options.text: Because males have two X chromosomes
Because colour blindness is caused by the Y chromosome
Because the Y chromosome does not carry a corresponding allele to mask the recessive one
Because females cannot inherit X-linked genes

questions.explanation: Males have only one X chromosome. If it carries the recessive allele for colour blindness, there is no second X chromosome with a dominant allele to mask it. Females need two copies of the recessive allele to be affected.

questions.stem: A carrier mother (who carries one colour blindness allele) and a normal father have a son. What is the chance the son will be colour blind?
questions.explanation: The carrier mother has genotype X^B X^b. Each son has a 50% chance of inheriting the X^b allele (and being colour blind) or the X^B allele (and having normal vision). The father's Y chromosome cannot mask the recessive allele.

questions.stem: How many autosomes (non-sex chromosomes) do humans have?

options.text: 20 pairs (40 chromosomes)
23 pairs (46 chromosomes)
22 pairs (44 chromosomes)
1 pair (2 chromosomes)

questions.explanation: Humans have 22 pairs of autosomes (44 autosomes) plus 1 pair of sex chromosomes, totalling 23 pairs (46 chromosomes). Autosomes carry genes for characteristics not related to sex determination.
